articles.title: A month of Sun days
articles.summary: Jane Houston Jones describes her month-long project observing and sketching the Sun, detailing her setup with a homemade dobsonian and H-alpha filter, and classifying various sunspots and active regions like AR0162 and AR0177. She highlights the educational aspect of solar observation and provides online resources for further study and verification. The document also includes the San Jose Astronomical Association's activity calendar for December and January, featuring star parties, ATM classes, and general meetings with speakers on topics like Mars exploration and celestial mapping.

articles.title: The shallow sky
articles.summary: This article offers a guide to celestial observations for December 2002, detailing positions and notable events for gas giants (Saturn, Jupiter, Uranus, Neptune) and inner planets (Mercury, Venus, Mars), including rare occurrences like mutual Jupiter moon eclipses and Saturn's proximity to the Crab nebula. It also includes an account of a special student visit to Lick Observatory and provides specific deep-sky targets for observers in the Bay Area, such as galaxies in Cetus, M77, and M33, accessible from dark sites like Henry Coe State Park.

articles.title: December Deep Sky
articles.summary: This article serves as an observing guide for December, detailing various deep-sky objects like galaxies, open clusters, planetary nebulae, and double stars, with tips for amateur astronomers using telescopes and binoculars. It also explores lunar rilles, explaining the formation of arcuate and sinuous types, while highlighting the mysterious and debated origins of straight rilles such as Rima Ariadaeus and Rima Sirsalis.

articles.title: Brow Furrows
articles.summary: This article, titled "Brow Furrows," defines rilles as challenging and interesting observational features on the Moon. It notes the Germanic origin of the word "rille," meaning "furrow," and introduces the three main types: arcuate, sinuous, and straight. While arcuate and sinuous rilles are associated with basaltic lavas, straight rilles remain a mystery.

articles.title: SJAA Loaner Scope Status
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) provides a telescope loaner program for its members, managed by Mike Koop. This article outlines the current status of various telescopes, categorizing them as immediately available, recently loaned out, or on extended loan. It also includes contact information for borrowing scopes and lists members on a waiting list for popular equipment.
